title: Collect the whole SDDC LCM task inventory from a spec-derived paginated contract
prompt:
Build a standard-library-only Python package that collects the complete VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 SDDC LCM task inventory and emits it in a stable, deterministic order. The inventory is a paginated collection: a single response is one page of it, and a caller that reads page zero and stops has silently lost most of the fleet's task history. Every page must be retrieved, and the assembled result must come out in the same order every run regardless of the order the service happened to return elements in.

The wire contract must be derived from the published OpenAPI specification -- `specifications/sddc-lcm/sddc-lcm-openapi.yaml` in the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository on GitHub, at commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba` -- and not from a documentation or reference web page. Retrieve that file and write `docs/contract.json` naming the exact operationIds `getTasks` and `getTask`, together with their methods, path templates, path and query parameters in specification order, request bodies and the `TaskStatus`, `PageMetadata` and `TaskSummary` schemas. Two details only the specification tells you: `getTasks` answers `500` with `PageOfTaskSummary` rather than the `ErrorResponse` every neighbouring operation returns, and the ceiling on `pageSize` is documented in that parameter's prose `description` instead of its schema, yet the client must honour it as the page size it falls back to. Record provenance in `docs/official_sources.json`: the repository, its SPDX licence, the spec path, the commit sha, the git blob sha and SHA-256 of the bytes you fetched, and every operationId used.

Then implement `src/vcf_sddc_lcm/contract.py` and `src/vcf_sddc_lcm/client.py` against that contract. The client builds every request target from the contract rather than from path literals, pages from `pageNumber` zero until `pageMetadata.totalPages` says it is done without refetching or overrunning, sorts by `startTime` then `id` while tolerating the summaries that have no `startTime` at all -- the spec marks only `id` as required -- and fetches the full `Task` for each `FAILED` summary. Above all it must distinguish a field the caller left unset from a field whose value is falsy: an unsupplied optional filter is absent from the query string entirely, while `pageNumber` `0` and an explicit `includeSystemTasks` `false` are values and go on the wire, the boolean spelled as JSON spells it. `includeSystemTasks` declares a schema default, and a default describes what the server does when the parameter is absent -- it is not licence to send it. `README.md` gives the exact contract shape and the full list of required wire behaviours.

Verification runs `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`, which starts a loopback mock pinned to your `docs/contract.json` -- it builds its routes and its query-parameter validation from the operations you named and serves nothing else -- and asserts the exact wire shape from the mock's request log, down to the percent-encoding of a date-time filter. Everything under `.protected/` is protected: read it and run it, but do not modify it. No VMware endpoint is contacted during verification.
network_rationale: the agent must retrieve the OpenAPI specification from github.com to derive the contract and to compute the content digests recorded in docs/official_sources.json; verification itself is loopback-only
scenario: five SDDC LCM task summaries arrive scrambled across three getTasks pages -- two sharing a startTime, one carrying none at all, two in FAILED -- and must be collected completely, ordered stably, and have their failures resolved through getTask, while the caller supplies some optional filters and leaves the rest unset
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves every page was fetched exactly once and none beyond the last, that pageNumber 0 and an explicit includeSystemTasks false were sent while every unset optional and the unsupplied schema default were omitted rather than sent empty, and that the date-time filter was percent-encoded intact
